about: contracts/order_create_prologue_refusals.json: the ten [status, code] pairs POST /agent/v2/orders answers ONLY before any order row of this request can be written: nine from the request's prologue, before the first call of the order write step, and one (MERCHANT_NOT_ACCEPTING_ORDERS) from inside the write step's function, above its order write. So no order row can exist because of this request when one is answered. That file is byte-identical to the agent gateway's copy (both sides pin its sha256). This file is this repository's own notes on how to read such an answer; tests/test_order_create_prologue_refusals_contract.py pins every statement in it.

envelope.note: The route's own code is error.details.error. error.code is derived from the HTTP status alone and is never a listed code. error.message equals error.details.error when the route named a code, and is otherwise a sentence.

PARTNER_ASSERTION_REJECTED.can_follow_an_accepted_earlier_copy_note: The same bytes delivered again after a copy was accepted, which may have created the order. `replay`: the nonce was already claimed. `stale`: the same, after the timestamp window closed. `subject`: the partner's agent record could not be read this time (a failed read counts as no agent) or the agent is no longer active; it is decided before the nonce is looked at, so it wins over `replay`. The nonce is kept longer than the window stays open, so an accepted request is never accepted twice by the store that claimed it. A caller holding a guard for the order should keep it on these three reasons.
PARTNER_ASSERTION_REJECTED.only_across_a_change_of_the_signing_secr: There is one signing secret and no previous-secret slot. A copy accepted under the old value and delivered again after the value changed (or was removed) is told `bad_mac` (or `no_secret`), not `replay`.
PARTNER_ASSERTION_REJECTED.subject_has_a_second_site: `subject` is also answered after the nonce was claimed, when the partner's agent record cannot be read at adoption. That is still before the route body.

MERCHANT_NOT_ACCEPTING_ORDERS.where: Listed at 403 only. Raised at two places inside the order write step's function, both above its order write: the merchant's status is one that takes no orders, or the order would be charged through the merchant's own payment provider and the merchant is not approved.
MERCHANT_NOT_ACCEPTING_ORDERS.after_a_written_row: Never answered for a quote that holds its order. Every create reads the quote's claim before any listed refusal of its own (POST /agent/v2/orders after its quote read, the order create with its parallel reads, right after its own replay), and the write step reads it again (read only, the caller and the quote, with no provider, intent or key in it) before either merchant refusal: a quote that holds an order is answered with that order, or 409 QUOTE_CONSUMED, and a claim that cannot be read is the retriable 503. A resend of the same create is answered with its order by the replay lookup before the write step is entered. The in-request busy retry runs the write step again only after a replay lookup that read the table found no order; a lookup that fails is the retriable 503 and the write step is not run again.
MERCHANT_NOT_ACCEPTING_ORDERS.residual_race: Two copies of one create in two processes (the per-merchant lock around the write step serialises copies within one process, and the second copy's claim read then sees the first copy's claim). The second copy's write step reads the merchant after its status changed, and reads the quote's claim before the first copy's order row is written (the read joins the claim to its order row, so a claim already written whose row is not yet there reads as no holder), while the first copy's write step is between its own merchant read and its order row (its quote revalidation, payment routing and store reads, then the claim insert: seconds under load). The second copy can then be told this code while the first copy makes the order. With the merchant still taking orders, the same window answers the second copy otherwise: its claim insert finds the first copy's claim, and the order is written under that one order id, which only one of the two writes. The replay lookup runs before that lock, so it does not close the window. Same class as PREFLIGHT_FAILED: a live read that can change between two copies, whose window is the first copy's whole create, because the pre-flight runs before the write step.

UNSUPPORTED_COMMERCE_PATH: Answered only after the order this create already made is answered (the cached answer, then the replay lookup), and after the quote's claim is read (a quote that holds its order is answered with it, or 409 QUOTE_CONSUMED), so a resend, or another create for the quote, after a store change does not get it. Residual race: a second copy in flight before the first copy's order row is written finds no replay and no holder, reads the store after it changed, and can be told this code while the first copy makes the order; the same class as PREFLIGHT_FAILED. A path that could not be decided (no active store, and the quote it is then read from could not be read) is the retriable 503 TEMPORARY_UNAVAILABLE with reason COMMERCE_PATH_UNKNOWN, never this code.
QUOTE_NOT_FOUND: Listed at 404 only (the caller does not own the quote, or it does not exist). The same code at 409 is the write step's own re-check of the quote, which can follow a written order, and at 400 is the pre-flight's; neither is listed.

not_listed_on_purpose.503 TEMPORARY_UNAVAILABLE: The database was busy, or it could not be told whether the order already exists (error.details.reason is then ORDER_REPLAY_LOOKUP_UNAVAILABLE or ORDER_QUOTE_GUARD_UNAVAILABLE), or the commerce path could not be decided (reason COMMERCE_PATH_UNKNOWN: the replay lookup and the quote's claim had already read the table and found no order of this create or for its quote; still not listed, as a 503 may also follow an order elsewhere in the request). An order may exist.
not_listed_on_purpose.409 QUOTE_CONSUMED: The quote already has its order.
not_listed_on_purpose.429: No 429 is listed, under any code. A resend of a create that was already accepted (the same signed bytes, or the same caller's create again) reaches the rate-limit middleware and the auth dependency's limits before the partner assertion's nonce is looked at, and (on POST /agent/v1/orders/create) the governance limit before the order replay lookup, so a 429 can be the answer while the first copy's order exists. Today the middleware's 429 names `rate_limit_exceeded` and the other limits answer a sentence.
